_comment: Ranking weighting lives here, NOT in code. Tune without touching the engine. The 9 weights sum to 1.0. Normalization bounds map each raw metric onto 0..1 before weighting.
_derivation: Weights fitted, not guessed. Method: 300 independently seeded synthetic seasons, each team carrying the latent `strength` the generator used; every metric normalized exactly as the engine does it; then maximize the correlation between the weighted score and true strength, subject to w >= 0 and sum(w) = 1, fitted on 66% of seasons and scored on the held-out 34%. Floors and caps keep the table publishable (results must visibly drive it, no single family may dominate). Held-out Spearman vs true strength: 0.69 with the previous hand-set weights, 0.76 with these. CAVEAT: the only ground truth available is the synthetic generator, so the phase metrics score better here than they would on real cricket, where a team's powerplay/death profile is a style choice and not a clean readout of overall quality. Re-fit these against real results once a season of live CricAPI data has accumulated.

_weightNotes.winPct: Held at the cap. Pure fit wanted far less, because a binary W/L over ~12 games is a noisy estimate of quality next to any season-averaged continuous measure. But a power ranking whose table does not visibly track winning is not publishable, so this carries a floor.
_weightNotes.powerplayDominance: Raised from 0.10. Phase measures are averaged over every ball of the season, so their sampling noise falls away far faster than win/loss does over a short season.
_weightNotes.deathOversNet: Raised from 0.10 — the strongest single correlate of team strength in the study (r = 0.87), matching what parameters.md predicted.
_weightNotes.rollingNRR: Trimmed from 0.15. Correlates 0.81 with form, so much of what it adds was already counted.
_weightNotes.form: Trimmed from 0.15. Correlates 0.76 with winPct; kept meaningful because movement and streaks are what the prose is written about.
_weightNotes.marginAdjustedWin: Cut from 0.10 to a floor. Measured correlation with strength was 0.007 — no signal AS CURRENTLY COMPUTED. It averages only over matches won and, for a chase, reads balls remaining out of 120, so a dominant side and a lucky one score alike. Worth re-weighting only after the metric itself is reworked.
_weightNotes.sos: Cut from 0.05 to a floor, and read the sign before raising it: in a complete round robin a team's opponents' average win% is close to the mirror of its own, which measured as r = -1.0 against strength. Adding it POSITIVELY therefore penalises the best teams. It only carries real information on an unbalanced schedule (internationals, or mid-season).
_weightNotes.keyPlayerAvailability: Held at 0.05 on domain grounds, not evidence. Star availability barely varies in the synthetic data (r = 0.08), so the study cannot see its value; parameters.md rates it a top real-world predictor. Revisit once a real ICC top-30 feed is wired.

_optionalNote: Extra metrics from parameters.md Groups 4-5. Off by default; toggle in the UI. Each contributes its weight to the score ONLY when enabled=true. Measured marginal value ON TOP OF the core 9: top4Consistency adds a little; expectedWins, chaseSet and tossLeverage add nothing measurable because they correlate 0.91, 0.95 and 0.80 with winPct, which is already weighted; bowlingConcentration showed no signal at all (r = -0.02). They are kept small so switching one on nudges the table rather than distorting it.

deathOvers._scalingNote: Converts bowling economy (runs/over) onto the batting strike-rate scale (runs/100 balls): 100/6 = 16.67. Net = deathBatSR - deathBowlEcon*scalingFactor.

_weightsNote: Hand-set editorial weights (2026-07-27). The previous values were fitted against synthetic seasons whose generator derived phase splits directly from team strength, which over-credited powerplay/death. Re-fit against REAL results once a live season exists.

match._note: Full T20 innings. Drives the ICC full-quota NRR rule and the win-quality runs conversion.

winQuality._note: Mean signed margin in RUNS over ALL matches (wins and losses).

scoreDisplay._note: Presentation band. The raw index (0-100) is mapped onto a published range by a FIXED affine transform, so it is stable week to week and strictly order-preserving — the ranking is untouched. Editorial choice for legibility, documented in power-rankings-explained.md.
